title: hollow-anchors-before-the-build-that-stands
owner: tester (hollow.py is the tester's instrument; the tester alone seals its readings)
intention: hollow reverts a ticket to the world before the build that stands, even when the ticket's BUILDME crossing was journaled after that build, and when it cannot find that world it says the anchor is wrong rather than blaming the chart.
why: The lived symptom: 68f563403c8f (the post-build reflection reaching codemother) is built, its proofs are green, and it cannot cross to PROVED, because hollow measured a world that already held the build and told the operator the chart was wrong. A reading that measured nothing and blamed the wrong leg sends the next mind to fix a chart that is right.
traces_to: Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass: the hollow reading is that proof's measurement, and one anchored inside the build measures nothing) and Law 7 (a record of truth may not collapse 'the anchor is wrong' into 'the chart is wrong'); Law 3 (the reading must say which world it measured)
how: Measured 2026-09-30: cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py:measure takes the anchor from _buildme_crossing (the LATEST forward BUILDME in the journals) and prebuild_commit (rev-list -1 --before=<at>). 68f563403c8f's build commit edb4e137 predates its only journaled BUILDME crossing (a bookkeeping re-cross after the artifact door opened), so the anchor aaa24fcc already holds the build, and hollow printed 'unwritten ... a finding against the chart's writes_to' for 4 of 4 files. That is the wrong cause on a record of truth (Law 7). Two changes. (1) The anchor becomes the EARLIER of the journaled crossing's pre-build commit and the parent of the earliest cairn commit that both names the ticket id in its message and changes a writes_to file, counted after the last back-edge out of BUILDME or PROVEME, so a re-cross with no build between keeps the build it followed; the reading records which rule chose the anchor ('journal' or 'first-build-commit') and both commits. (2) When every measured-eligible file is byte-identical at the chosen anchor, measure raises HollowUnmeasurable naming the anchor as postdating the build, instead of reporting each file as unwritten. Then rerun `cairn test --hollow 68f563403c8f --seal` and recompute the clearance lacks.
falsifier: RED if after the build: (1) in a scratch repo whose build commit precedes its journaled BUILDME crossing, measure reverts to a commit containing the build; (2) in a scratch repo with a kickback and a rebuild, measure reverts to before the FIRST build rather than the rebuild; (3) a run where every eligible file is identical at the anchor returns a reading instead of raising HollowUnmeasurable naming the anchor; (4) the sealed evidence.hollow reading lacks anchor_rule ('journal' | 'first-build-commit') and both candidate commits; (5) live, `cairn test --hollow 68f563403c8f` measures 0 files. WRONG INTENT if Akien answers that a build committed before its journaled crossing must be rebuilt, not measured. Horizon: the live 68f5 run right after the build commit.
watchme: none, because the falsifier's live half is a single run that either measures 68f563403c8f's files or does not (CairnCommons/troubles/boat-crossed-to-proved-uncovered-68f563403c8f.json clears or stands on it), and every later hollow run seals its anchor_rule on the reading, so there is nothing further to learn by watching
builder_check: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Where? cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py: a new `_first_build_commit(tid, files, since_at, repo_root)` runs `git log --reverse --format=%H --grep=<tid> --since=<last back-edge at, or none> -- <files>` and returns the first hash or None; measure() takes `commit = prebuild_commit(at)`, and if the first build commit exists and is an ancestor of that commit (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`), it uses `<first>^` instead and sets anchor_rule='first-build-commit'. Otherwise anchor_rule='journal'. (2) Where does the last back-edge come from? The same journals buildme_crossing reads: the latest entry for this ticket whose direction is back out of BUILDME or PROVEME, before the chosen BUILDME crossing; none means no bound. (3) What does the reading gain? `anchor: {rule, commit, journal_commit, first_build_commit}`, sealed with the rest through record_hollow. (4) The unmeasurable case? After the per-file loop, if measured is empty and every non-skipped file was UNWRIT, raise HollowUnmeasurable('hollow: every eligible file is identical at <commit> — the anchor postdates the build, not the chart'); the cli already prints HollowUnmeasurable and exits nonzero. (5) Proof? cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_hollow_anchor.py, three teeth over scratch git repos built in tmp dirs with a scratch journal: build-before-crossing anchors at the build's parent; kickback-and-rebuild anchors at the rebuild's parent; all-identical raises. Sealed by the tester. (6) Then run `cairn test --hollow 68f563403c8f --seal` live and recompute the clearance lacks.
